note: SortedSetRankBenchmarks (BenchmarkDotNet, default job), before and after the 1.1 order-statistic tree. 'before' is the 1.0 SortedSet<T>-backed store, whose rank queries count from one end; 'after' is the AVL tree with subtree sizes. The probe is the middle member, where an O(n) walk costs most - a top-N query would hide the difference.
reading: Rank and rank-range become independent of set size (12.7 ms -> 145 ns at a million members). Score ranges, already O(log n), are unchanged within noise. Rescoring - the order-book write - is about 10% slower, the cost of maintaining subtree sizes on every insert and delete. The 1.0 run at 1,000 members was not captured.
